# pki_cert_request (Data Source)

Decodes a certificate signing request that arrived from elsewhere — a device, another team, a Kubernetes Secret — and reports its contents for inspection or assertion before issuing.

Unlike the resource of the same name, this data source does not create anything: it reads an existing CSR. A CSR whose signature does not verify is reported as `signature_valid = false` rather than raised as an error, because refusing to decode it would hide the only signal that matters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Inspect a CSR handed over by a device or another team before signing it.
data "pki_cert_request" "incoming" {
  content_pem = file("device.csr")
}

# Refuse to issue against a CSR whose signature does not verify, or whose
# common name is outside the domain this CA is willing to sign for.
resource "pki_certificate" "device" {
  count = data.pki_cert_request.incoming.signature_valid ? 1 : 0

  ca_certificate_pem = var.ca_certificate_pem
  ca_private_key_pem = var.ca_private_key_pem
  csr_pem            = data.pki_cert_request.incoming.content_pem
  validity           = "8760h"

  # Extensions always come from here, never from the CSR.
  key_usage {
    usages = ["digitalSignature", "keyEncipherment"]
  }
  extended_key_usage {
    usages = ["clientAuth"]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `content_base64` (String) The CSR's DER, standard base64-encoded, so material read straight out of a Kubernetes Secret needs no decoding step. Exactly one of `content_pem` and `content_base64` must be set.
- `content_pem` (String) The CSR as a PEM `CERTIFICATE REQUEST` block. Exactly one of `content_pem` and `content_base64` must be set.

### Read-Only

- `public_key_algorithm` (String) The public key's algorithm: `RSA`, `ECDSA`, or `ED25519`.
- `public_key_pem` (String) The CSR's public key, PKIX-encoded (`PUBLIC KEY`).
- `requested_extensions` (Attributes List) Every extension the CSR carries, in declaration order, including the SAN. Each is reported unparsed — as its OID, criticality, and the raw base64 of its `extnValue` — so nothing is lost to a parser this data source does not have, and a caller can see extensions the typed `san` block does not surface. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--requested_extensions))
- `san` (Attributes) The `subjectAltName` extension, decoded into its four GeneralName types. Null when the CSR carries no subjectAltName. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--san))
- `signature_algorithm` (String) The signature algorithm the request carries, one of `ECDSA-SHA256`, `ECDSA-SHA384`, `ECDSA-SHA512`, `Ed25519`, `SHA256-RSA`, `SHA256-RSAPSS`, `SHA384-RSA`, `SHA384-RSAPSS`, `SHA512-RSA`, `SHA512-RSAPSS`.
- `signature_valid` (Boolean) Whether the request's self-signature verifies. A `false` value is **data, not an error**: the whole point of this data source is to surface it so the caller can refuse to issue against a request whose signature does not check out.
- `subject` (Attributes List) The request's subject DN as a list of `{oid, value, string_type}` objects in declaration order — the only order a parser can report, because the DN's attribute order is part of its bytes. `string_type` is always populated, so a caller comparing two requests sees the ASN.1 encoding each attribute carries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subject))

<a id="nestedatt--requested_extensions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `requested_extensions`

Required:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `oid` (String) Dotted-decimal OID of the extension.
- `value_base64` (String) Standard base64 of the extension's raw DER `extnValue` (the OCTET STRING content, not the whole `Extension` SEQUENCE).


<a id="nestedatt--san"></a>
### Nested Schema for `san`

Read-Only:

- `critical` (Boolean) Whether the extension is marked critical.
- `dns_names` (List of String) `dNSName` entries, in declaration order.
- `email_addresses` (List of String) `rfc822Name` entries, in declaration order.
- `ip_addresses` (List of String) `iPAddress` entries as plain addresses (`10.0.0.5`, `fd00::5`), in declaration order.
- `uris` (List of String) `uniformResourceIdentifier` entries, in declaration order.


<a id="nestedatt--subject"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subject`

Required:

- `oid` (String) Dotted-decimal OID of the DN attribute type.
- `string_type` (String) The ASN.1 string encoding of `value`: one of `utf8`, `bmp`, `ia5`, `printable`, `t61`. Always populated, including for the `utf8` default.
- `value` (String) The attribute's value.
